newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were steady to $0.50 per cwt lower amid continued ample hog supplies, dealers and packer buyers said.
Declines were tempered by firm demand from several packers looking to fill out live inventories, particularly in the eastern Corn Belt, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $55.00 to $55.50 at country buying stations and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, sources there said.
"We've got a pretty good run of hogs so far this morning," said one packer buyer who buys in Iowa/southern Minnesota.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.00 to $55.50 at plants, but could turn higher if packer demand increases, dealers said.
"Demand is good right now, and could get better as the day goes along," an Illinois dealer said.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower amid adequate hog marketings at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.50 to $56.00 at plants, sources there said.
Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $53.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.50 to $56.00 at plants, dealers there said.
